title: Senior Paid Media & Performance Marketing Manager (B2B SaaS)
description:
High Point International Inc. helps B2B SaaS executives build high-conviction growth engines. We are looking for an analytical, hands-on growth strategist to bridge the gap between ad spend and bottom-line revenue.



Mission



Drive scalable pipeline growth for B2B SaaS clients by executing full-funnel paid media campaigns and establishing closed-loop CRM attribution. You will solve tracking blind spots, optimize multi-channel performance, and deliver clear, data-backed acquisition strategies that translate marketing investments into qualified demos, pipeline, and predictable revenue.



What You'll Do



- Build, manage, and optimize multi-channel paid acquisition campaigns across Google Search, Demand Gen, LinkedIn, Meta, and emerging platforms like OpenAI Ads, Reddit, and CTV.



- Establish end-to-end tracking and attribution integrity using Google Tag Manager, GA4, UTM frameworks, and CRM integrations (HubSpot/Salesforce) to connect ad interactions directly to pipeline and revenue.



- Conduct continuous channel experimentation, evaluating new platforms for audience fit, cost efficiency, creative requirements, and measurement capabilities.



- Manage campaign mechanics including targeting, keyword strategy, bid structures, budget allocation, and continuous creative/landing page testing.



- Translate complex performance data into clear narrative reporting for executive stakeholders, highlighting CAC, opportunity creation, ROI, and strategic next steps.



- Collaborate cross-functionally with creative, content, and web teams to design high-converting ad assets and landing page experiences tailored to ICP decision-makers.



What Success Looks Like



- High-trust tracking environments established across clients, ensuring 100% data alignment between ad platforms, analytics tools, and CRM pipeline reports.



- Shift in focus from vanity metrics (clicks/leads) to full-funnel efficiency, resulting in reduced CAC and higher demo-to-opportunity conversion rates.



- Clear experimental roadmap active at all times, leading to early adoption of profitable new acquisition channels.



- Executive-ready reporting delivered regularly, providing clear recommendations on where to scale, optimize, or reallocate ad spend.



Nice to Have



- Hands-on experience with emerging ad platforms like OpenAI Ads, Reddit, or CTV.



- Deep familiarity with enterprise B2B sales cycles, ABM frameworks, and public sector/enterprise SaaS marketing.



- Advanced experience with offline conversion tracking and custom CRM data synchronization.



Logistics



- Location: Remote

- Weekly Hours: 20 hours/week

* Respond to customer inquiries in a timely and professional manner.

 Groups).

* Fluent English (written and spoken).

* Previous experience in customer support, customer service, or call center roles (required).

title: Website Designer with personality (Figma), part-time, for health and wellness brands
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE



I run a small Australian studio that creates brand strategies and websites for health and wellness businesses: dietitians, psychologists, physios, midwives and clinics.



Every one of my clients is a real person with a story, a sense of humour and their own way of doing things. I want their website to feel like meeting them. If the logo could be swapped for any other clinic's and nobody would notice, the design isn't finished.



I do the strategy, write the copy and build the sites in Webflow. You'll own how they look: moodboards, website designs and brand pieces in Figma.





THE DESIGN I LOVE



- Warm and editorial, with one memorable idea on every page

- Confident type, interesting layouts and space used on purpose

- Colour with a point of view

- Photos chosen and cropped with care

- Small details that could only belong to that client



Pretty templates are easy to find. I'm looking for your ideas.





HOW A PROJECT WORKS



1. You get a written brief, the real copy, photos, brand files and a few sites the client and I love.

2. Moodboards: two options, with colours, fonts and layout ideas. We agree on the direction before you design a page.

3. Homepage: desktop and mobile, with one round of revisions.

4. Section designs: reusable sections I build the other pages from.

5. Handover: a tidy Figma file with named layers, styles and exported images.



Every stage has an agreed time and due date before you start.





HOW WE WORK TOGETHER



- Ask questions early. If you're going to miss a due date, message me as soon as you know.

- On days you work for me, send a short update.

- Text needs good contrast and must be easy to read on a phone.

- Reply within one working day, Monday to Friday, with some overlap with 9am to 3pm AEST.





HOW TO APPLY



1. Start your application with the word "Lantern".

2. Send your portfolio and point me to ONE website you designed that could only belong to that client. Tell me what makes it theirs.

3. Send one website you love that you didn't design, and tell me why.

4. Tell me how long two moodboards and a homepage (desktop and mobile) usually take you.

5. Tell me your weekly availability, and confirm that A$12 an hour works for you.



Please write your answers yourself. I'd love to hear how you think.





NEXT STEP



Shortlisted designers do a short paid test for a sample client: one moodboard and one hero section. You'll get a description of the client's personality and three reference sites. We'll agree on the moodboard before you start the hero, and the time is capped at 3 hours.

title: Social Media & Lead Vetting Specialist (Makati)
description:
Part-Time Social Media & Lead Vetting Specialist (B2B Trade Software)

 

Location Makati / Metro Manila – work from home, occasional in-person meetings in Makati

Hours Part-time, approx. 20 hours per week, flexible

Pay AUD 900 – 1,100 per month (based on experience)

Engagement Independent contractor, paid monthly

Start Prep phase first (no public posting), then live posting timed with our new software releases

Reports to The founder (Australia)

About us

We are a small Australian software company with a very niche product: stock control for cabinetmakers, joiners, shopfitters and stone fabricators. Our Ezy range (OffcutEzy, EdgeEzy, ProfileEzy, SlabEzy and others) tracks high-value partial materials that normal ERP systems ignore: sheet offcuts, edgebanding rolls, aluminium extrusions and stone slab remnants.

Until now every sale has come from word of mouth, and we have almost no online presence. We want a steady, manageable flow of the right customers, not rapid growth. Quality of each lead matters far more than the number of leads.

The role

You will build and run our social media presence from scratch and act as the gatekeeper for new enquiries. You d
 how to do it; the founder approves the content and meets only the leads you have fully vetted.

• Channels:
 first (our page plus Australian trade groups). LinkedIn second, mainly for researching and contacting decision-makers.

• Voice: you post and engage openly as our company's representative, never as a fake customer or under a false identity.

• Two halves, equally important: creating good content, and filtering enquiries so only genuine, qualified prospects reach the founder.

Getting started – two phases

1. Prep phase (before our new releases): set up and brand the pages without promoting them yet. Research and join the trade groups and learn how they work. Build the prospect list, tracker, qualification form and message templates. Draft the first 1–2 months of content ready for approval.

2. Live phase (shortly before and after release): start posting, engaging in groups and vetting enquiries.

The timing of the switch depends on our software release dates, so you need to be comfortable with a flexible timeline.

Key responsibilities

1. Set up our presence. Create and brand our
 business page and LinkedIn company page. Find and join the right Australian trade
 groups and check each group's rules on promotion.

2. Plan and create content. Prepare a monthly content calendar of 3 posts per week. Turn our workshop photos and software screenshots into "From This to This" before-and-after graphics: messy offcut racks, loose edgebanding and wasted stone versus our clean software dashboard. Write the captions.

3. Get approval in batches. Send the whole month's posts to the founder in one batch for sign-off. Get the FAQ answers and message templates approved once, then use them freely. Anything off-script goes to the founder first.

4. Engage in the community. Check target groups on most working days. Join real conversations about material waste and workshop bottlenecks, help first and never spam or hard-sell.

5. Source prospects. Research Australian cabinetmakers, joiners, shopfitters and stone fabricators with a commercial workshop who are likely to be losing track of materials.

6. Vet every enquiry. Use our qualification questions by message or a short online form to check each prospect before anything goes to the founder.

7. Hand over and report. Log every lead in a shared tracker with company details, contact, pain points and notes. Send the founder a short weekly report and book qualified prospects into his calendar.

Lead qualification (no tyre kickers)

A lead is passed to the founder as Qualified only when it meets all four checks:

Check What it means

Decision-maker Business owner, director, or workshop/operations manager

Business type Cabinetmaker, joiner, shopfitter or stone fabricator with a physical commercial workshop holding raw stock (not mobile handymen or flat-pack installers)

Material pain Says they struggle to track, or are wasting, costly materials: sheet offcuts, aluminium lengths, edgebanding rolls or stone remnants

Intent Agrees to a follow-up conversation with the founder, not just asking "how much?" in the comments

A lead that passes the first two checks but not yet the last two goes on a separate Warm list. You keep in light contact with these, and the founder sees the list in the weekly report. Anyone who fails the first two checks is politely closed off.

How success is measured

We want a small, steady pipeline: about one new customer a month, not a flood of leads. These targets apply once the live phase starts and are reviewed after its first 2 months. During the prep phase, success means everything is ready to go on time.

Measure Monthly target

Approved posts published on time 12 or more (3 per week)

Enquiries answered Within 1 working day

Qualified leads handed to the founder 2 – 4 (no more than 4 without the founder's OK)

Weekly report sent Every Friday

Content or messages published without approval Zero

Working arrangement

• Part-time and flexible: around 20 hours a week. Some hours should fall between 8am and 1pm Manila time (10am–3pm Australian Eastern), when our customers and the founder are active.

• Approvals in batches: one monthly content sign-off, plus quick approval for anything new. No daily hand-holding.

• Meetings: an in-person meeting in Makati can be arranged for onboarding and reviews. Day-to-day work is from home.

• Paid trial: the first 4 weeks of the prep phase are a paid trial covering page set-up, the group research, the tracker and a first batch of draft posts.

• Payment: monthly, in AUD or PHP equivalent, by bank transfer or Wise.

• Rules of the road: follow each group's rules and LinkedIn's messaging limits, and Australia's anti-spam rules for cold outreach. All customer details stay confidential.

What you need

Essential

• 2+ years managing business
 pages and groups engagement for a B2B company, with LinkedIn experience a plus

• Proven lead generation or screening experience: qualifying prospects by message or chat and filtering out time-wasters

• Canva (or similar): clean graphics that combine real photos with software screenshots

• Excellent written English that sounds natural and direct to Australian tradespeople, not corporate

• Strict discipline with approvals: nothing goes public without sign-off

• Self-managed and organised: keeps a tracker up to date and reports without being chased

• Reliable internet and your own laptop

Highly regarded

• Knowledge of the Australian building, joinery, CNC manufacturing or stone industries

• Experience with a simple CRM, Google Sheets, Google Forms and Calendly

• Experience building a page or community from zero followers

How to apply

Send a short CV, 2–3 examples of social media or lead generation work, and your expected monthly rate. Please also complete this short task (about 30 minutes). Applications without it will not be considered.

1. Reply to a group post. An Australian cabinetmaker posts in a
 group: "Our offcut rack is a disaster again. Half of it ends up in the skip because no one knows what's there." Write the comment you would post as our representative.

2. Vet a lead. Someone comments "How much is it?" under one of our posts. Write the direct message you would send to find out whether they are worth passing to the founder.

3. One post idea. Describe in 2–3 lines a "From This to This" post you would create for stone slab remnants.

Shortlisted applicants will have a video call and, where possible, a meeting in Makati.

Notes for the founder (delete before posting)

• Pay check: AUD 900–1,100 for about 20 hours a week works out at roughly AUD 10–13 an hour. That is a solid part-time rate in Metro Manila and should attract experienced applicants.

• Phased start: the ad now has a prep phase before any public posting, because the new app versions are not released yet. D
 whether prep is paid at the full rate or at fewer hours, for example 10 hours a week.

• Lead cap: the 2–4 qualified leads a month, capped at 4, keeps you busy without overloading you. Raise or lower it any time.

• Customer size: the original brief targeted mid-to-large workshops, while the Turno proposal assumed about 10 staff. The ad doesn't set a size, so tell me if you want one added.

• Lessons from the Turno proposal: it was well written and well structured, but it didn't deliver. The paid trial and the written test task check real work rather than how good a pitch looks. It would help to note what went wrong last time so we can screen for it.

• Company name: the ad names the Ezy products but not the company. Add the name if you're happy for applicants to see it.

• Where to post: OnlineJobs.ph is the main board for Philippine remote staff. JobStreet PH and LinkedIn also work for Makati-based candidates.

title: Virtual Operations Assistant – SOP Development & Training Coordinator
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION



Virtual Operations Assistant – SOP Development, Training & Operations Management



Company: Dumpster Rental, Junk Removal, Demolition & Excavation

Position: Virtual Operations Assistant – SOP Development & Training Coordinator

Department: Operations / Administration / Virtual Call Center

Employment Type: Full-Time

Work Arrangement: Remote / Virtual

Reports To: Business Owner / Operations Manager



⸻



1. POSITION OVERVIEW



We are seeking a highly organized, proactive, detail-oriented, and technology-savvy Virtual Operations Assistant to help build, document, organize, and manage the operational systems of our growing businesses.



The primary responsibility of this position will be to help establish and develop the operational infrastructure for our virtual call center supporting Dumpster Rental, Junk Removal, Demolition & Excavation.



This individual will play an important role in building the foundation of our virtual team by learning every aspect of the company’s back-office operations, documenting processes, creating Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), developing training materials, and assisting with the onboarding and training of new Virtual Assistants.



Our initial objective is to hire and develop a team of 3–4 Virtual Assistants who will handle inbound customer calls, outbound calling campaigns, lead follow-up, scheduling, and administrative responsibilities.



The Virtual Operations Assistant will be responsible for helping us turn our daily business processes into organized, repeatable, documented systems so that new team members can be trained efficiently and perform their responsibilities consistently.



This is not simply a data-entry or general administrative position. We are looking for someone who enjoys building systems, improving workflows, organizing information, creating training materials, and helping a business grow.



As the call center becomes established and the initial team is fully trained, this position will expand into supporting the development and operational organization of our digital marketing company.



The long-term objective is to have this individual become a key part of our company’s operational infrastructure, helping develop SOPs, workflows, training systems, and processes across multiple business operations.



2. PRIMARY OBJECTIVES OF THE POSITION



The successful candidate will be responsible for accomplishing the following objectives:



1. Learn and understand every important aspect of the back-office operations of Dumpster Rental, Junk Removal, Demolition & Excavation.

2. Document existing business processes and turn them into clear, step-by-step Standard Operating Procedures.

3. Create video tutorials and screen-recorded training demonstrations for company systems and administrative processes.

4. Assist in recruiting coordination, onboarding, and training new Virtual Assistants.

5. Help establish a structured virtual call center with 3–4 trained inbound and outbound agents.

6. Develop a centralized SOP and training library that employees can reference independently.

7. Monitor workflows and help ensure that Virtual Assistants follow established procedures.

8. Identify operational inefficiencies and recommend improvements.

9. Assist with the development of administrative workflows, reporting systems, and internal communication procedures.

10. Eventually assist in documenting and developing the SOPs and operational workflows for our digital marketing agency.



3. PHASE ONE: LEARNING THE BUSINESS & BACK-OFFICE OPERATIONS



During the initial training period, the Operations Assistant must become familiar with the company’s business model, services, administrative systems, customer journey, and internal workflows.



The expectation is that this person will learn how the business operates from the moment a potential customer contacts us until the job is completed and the customer has been followed up with.



Responsibilities include:



A. Understanding Company Services



Become familiar with the company’s services, including:



* Junk removal.

* Residential and commercial cleanouts.

* Property cleanouts.

* Construction debris removal.

* Demolition services.

* Excavation services.

* Land clearing and related services.

* Other services offered by the company.



Understand the basic information customers need, common customer questions, the types of jobs the company accepts, and when a call should be transferred to management for additional information or pricing approval.



The Operations Assistant does not need to independently perform demolition or excavation estimating. However, they must understand the service offerings well enough to train agents to communicate professionally and collect the correct information from customers.



B. Learning All Back-Office Systems



The Operations Assistant will receive training on the company’s administrative systems and must become proficient in using them.



This may include:



* Business phone systems and call-routing platforms.

* CRM and lead management systems.

*
 and communication platforms.

* Scheduling and calendar management.

* Customer databases.

* Lead tracking and follow-up systems.

* Quoting and estimating workflows.

* Job scheduling and dispatch procedures.

* Administrative documentation.

* File management and cloud storage.

* Invoicing and payment coordination procedures.

* Customer service processes.

* Internal reporting and performance tracking.



The goal is to understand how information moves through the business and how each system connects to the next.



The Operations Assistant will eventually be responsible for documenting these systems so that new Virtual Assistants can learn them without requiring constant one-on-one supervision.



4. PHASE TWO: STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES (SOP) DEVELOPMENT



One of the most important responsibilities of this position is creating a complete library of Standard Operating Procedures.



The Operations Assistant will work directly with the business owner and management to identify processes that need to be documented.



A. Creating Written SOPs



Create clear, organized, step-by-step instructions for daily business operations.



Examples include:



* How to answer incoming customer calls.

* How to identify and qualify potential customers.

* How to collect customer contact information.

* How to document job details.

* How to enter leads into the CRM.

* How to schedule estimates or appointments.

* How to follow up with potential customers.

* How to conduct outbound sales calls.

* How to handle missed calls and voi
s.

* How to respond to customer inquiries.

* How to manage customer complaints.

* How to transfer calls to management.

* How to update customer records.

* How to organize company files.

* How to complete daily administrative tasks.

* How to prepare daily and weekly reports.



Each SOP should include:



1. The purpose of the procedure.

2. When the procedure should be used.

3. The person responsible for completing it.

4. The tools or software required.

5. Step-by-step instructions.

6. Screenshots or visual examples when appropriate.

7. Common mistakes to avoid.

8. Escalation procedures when an issue cannot be resolved.

9. A checklist to confirm the task has been completed correctly.



B. Video SOPs and Screen-Recording Tutorials



The Operations Assistant will be responsible for creating video-based training materials.



This will involve recording their computer screen while demonstrating how to complete specific tasks.



Examples include:



* How to navigate the CRM.

* How to enter a new lead.

* How to answer and transfer calls.

* How to schedule appointments.

* How to update customer information.

* How to complete administrative workflows.

* How to manage outbound calling lists.

* How to document customer interactions.

* How to prepare reports.



Videos should be organized, easy to understand, and broken into individual topics rather than creating long, confusing recordings.



The objective is to create a video training library that allows new Virtual Assistants to watch, learn, and repeat each process independently.



The Operations Assistant should be comfortable using screen-recording software, editing basic video tutorials, adding explanations, and organizing the finished videos into a centralized training library.



5. PHASE THREE: VIRTUAL ASSISTANT HIRING, ONBOARDING & TRAINING



Once the foundational SOPs are created, the Operations Assistant will assist with bringing on 3–4 Virtual Assistants to build the company’s virtual call center.



The Operations Assistant will help coordinate and facilitate the onboarding and training process.



A. New Employee Onboarding



Responsibilities include:



* Preparing onboarding materials.

* Organizing training documents.

* Providing new employees with access to approved company systems.

* Explaining company procedures and expectations.

* Introducing new hires to the company’s services.

* Providing access to video SOPs.

* Walking new employees through their daily responsibilities.

* Ensuring new employees understand communication standards.

* Explaining reporting requirements.

* Tracking training progress.

* Maintaining onboarding checklists.



B. Training Inbound Call Agents



Assist in training Virtual Assistants responsible for receiving incoming customer calls.



Training topics will include:



* Professional phone etiquette.

* Answering calls using the company greeting.

* Understanding the company’s services.

* Identifying the customer’s needs.

* Asking the correct qualifying questions.

* Collecting customer contact information.

* Documenting job details.

* Entering leads into the CRM.

* Scheduling estimates or appointments.

* Transferring calls when necessary.

* Handling common customer questions.

* Following up on missed calls.

* Knowing when to escalate questions to management.



C. Training Outbound Call Agents



Assist in training Virtual Assistants responsible for making outbound calls.



Training topics will include:



* Understanding outbound calling campaigns.

* Following approved calling scripts.

* Contacting potential customers and leads.

* Following up with previous inquiries.

* Calling customers who requested estimates.

* Following up on outstanding estimates.

* Contacting approved referral or business prospects.

* Recording call outcomes.

* Updating lead statuses in the CRM.

* Scheduling follow-up calls.

* Maintaining professional communication.

* Following applicable calling, consent, and do-not-call requirements.



D. Training Administrative Assistants



Some Virtual Assistants may also perform administrative responsibilities.



The Operations Assistant will help train them on:



* Data entry.

* Updating CRM records.

* Organizing customer information.

* Managing
 correspondence.

* Updating spreadsheets.

* Scheduling appointments.

* Preparing reports.

* Organizing digital files.

* Managing follow-up reminders.

* Completing assigned back-office tasks.



E. Training Quality Control



The Operations Assistant will help evaluate whether new Virtual Assistants understand their responsibilities and can perform tasks independently.



This includes:



* Reviewing completed training assignments.

* Checking whether employees follow SOPs.

* Conducting practice exercises.

* Reviewing sample call documentation.

* Identifying knowledge gaps.

* Providing additional training when necessary.

* Updating training materials when recurring problems occur.

* Reporting employee training progress to management.



The goal is to create a repeatable onboarding system so that future employees can be trained using established procedures rather than starting from scratch each time.



6. PHASE FOUR: ONGOING OPERATIONS SUPPORT & WORKFLOW MANAGEMENT



Once the initial team of 3–4 Virtual Assistants has been hired and trained, the Operations Assistant will transition into helping maintain and improve the company’s daily operating systems.



Responsibilities will include:



A. SOP Maintenance



* Keep SOPs updated as business processes change.

* Create new SOPs when new tasks are introduced.

* Update outdated video tutorials.

* Organize training resources.

* Maintain version control of important documents.

* Ensure employees have access to the latest procedures.



B. Workflow Organization



* Help establish clear daily workflows for each Virtual Assistant.

* Organize task assignments.

* Create checklists for recurring responsibilities.

* Help streamline communication between agents and management.

* Identify bottlenecks and repetitive tasks.

* Recommend ways to improve efficiency.

* Help establish accountability systems.



C. Performance Tracking



Assist management in monitoring operational performance through reports and tracking systems.



Potential performance indicators include:



* Number of inbound calls received.

* Number of calls answered.

* Missed calls.

* Outbound calls completed.

* Leads generated.

* Leads successfully entered into the CRM.

* Follow-up tasks completed.

* Appointments scheduled.

* Customer inquiries requiring escalation.

* Administrative tasks completed.

* Employee training completion.

* SOP compliance.



The Operations Assistant will help compile and organize this information for management review.



D. Internal Communication



Help establish organized communication procedures between the Virtual Assistants, management, and the business owner.



This includes:



* Communicating important process updates.

* Sharing revised SOPs.

* Organizing internal announcements.

* Following up on assigned operational tasks.

* Helping employees find answers to procedural questions.

* Escalating recurring operational issues.

* Keeping management informed of training and workflow concerns.



7. PHASE FIVE: DIGITAL MARKETING AGENCY OPERATIONS DEVELOPMENT



After the initial call center team has been successfully hired, trained, and established, the position will gradually expand to assist with building the operational infrastructure of our digital marketing company.



This will represent the next stage of growth and responsibility.



The Operations Assistant will work with management to help document, organize, and develop repeatable workflows for the digital marketing agency.



Potential responsibilities will include:



A. Digital Marketing Agency SOP Development



Help create SOPs for:



* New client onboarding.

* Client information collection.

* Client account setup.

* Project management.

* Task assignments.

* Client communication.

* Content creation workflows.

* Social media management.

* Digital advertising campaign coordination.

* Website project coordination.

* Lead generation processes.

* Client reporting.

* Monthly performance reporting.

* Client follow-up procedures.



B. Agency Workflow Development



Help establish organized workflows for the various functions of the marketing agency.



This may include:



* Creating task management systems.

* Organizing client folders and documentation.

* Developing employee onboarding procedures.

* Creating quality-control checklists.

* Documenting project handoff procedures.

* Organizing recurring client deliverables.

* Establishing reporting procedures.

* Documenting communication standards.

* Helping coordinate administrative workflows.



C. Building Scalable Systems



The long-term goal is to help create a digital marketing agency that can grow by adding employees, contractors, and clients without having to reinvent its operating procedures each time.



The Operations Assistant will help document how work is completed, who is responsible for each task, and how employees should communicate and report their progress.



This position will gradually become involved in operational development across both businesses as the companies grow.



8. REQUIRED SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS



We are looking for someone who has a combination of administrative experience, organizational skills, technical ability, and a strong interest in business operations.



Essential Qualifications



* Previous experience as a Virtual Assistant, Administrative Assistant, Operations Assistant, or similar position.

* Excellent written and spoken English.

* Strong organizational and time-management skills.

* Ability to learn new software and technology quickly.

* Excellent attention to detail.

* Strong written communication skills.

* Ability to create clear instructions and documentation.

* Comfortable recording screen tutorials and training videos.

* Ability to explain processes to other employees.

* Strong problem-solving skills.

* Ability to work independently.

* Ability to manage multiple projects and responsibilities.

* Comfortable communicating with management and team members.

* Willingness to learn all aspects of a business operation.



Technical Skills



Experience with some or all of the following is preferred:



* Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Drive, Gmail).

* Microsoft Office.

* CRM platforms.

* Business phone and VoIP systems.

* Video recording software.

* Screen-recording and tutorial creation.

* Project management platforms.

* Cloud-based file management.

* Spreadsheets and reporting.

* AI productivity tools.

* Workflow automation tools.



Experience with tools such as Loom, Google Drive, Notion, ClickUp, Trello, Slack, or similar platforms is a plus.



The candidate does not need to know every platform before starting, but must be comfortable learning new systems.



9. PERSONALITY & WORK ETHIC



The ideal candidate will be someone who:



* Takes initiative instead of waiting to be told what to do.

* Enjoys organizing businesses and creating systems.

* Is naturally detail-oriented.

* Likes teaching and helping others succeed.

* Can recognize when a process is inefficient.

* Is comfortable asking questions when something is unclear.

* Takes ownership of assigned responsibilities.

* Is dependable and consistent.

* Can handle constructive feedback.

* Is comfortable working in a growing business environment.

* Understands the importance of confidentiality.

* Wants to grow professionally with the company.



We are looking for someone who thinks beyond completing individual tasks and understands how those tasks fit into the larger operation of a business.



The right candidate should have a systems-oriented mindset and take pride in creating processes that make a company more organized, efficient, and scalable.



10. FIRST 90-DAY EXPECTATIONS



The first 90 days will focus on learning the business, documenting processes, and establishing the foundation for the virtual call center.



Days 1–30: Learning & Documentation



Primary focus:



* Learn the company’s services and operations.

* Become familiar with all back-office systems.

* Understand the customer journey.

* Learn inbound and outbound call processes.

* Learn administrative procedures.

* Begin documenting existing workflows.

* Identify processes that require SOPs.

* Begin creating written SOPs and video tutorials.



Expected deliverables:



* Initial back-office operations overview.

* Inventory of systems and software.

* Initial SOP library.

* Initial collection of screen-recorded tutorials.

* List of processes requiring additional documentation.



Days 31–60: SOP Development & Team Onboarding



Primary focus:



* Expand the SOP library.

* Complete core call center procedures.

* Create training materials.

* Assist with hiring coordination.

* Begin onboarding new Virtual Assistants.

* Conduct training sessions.

* Help employees practice inbound and outbound calling procedures.

* Establish training checklists.



Expected deliverables:



* Completed core call center SOPs.

* Organized video training library.

* New-hire onboarding checklist.

* Inbound call training procedures.

* Outbound call training procedures.

* Administrative training materials.

* Employee training progress tracker.



Days 61–90: Team Development & Operational Organization



Primary focus:



* Assist in completing training for the initial 3–4 Virtual Assistants.

* Evaluate employee readiness.

* Identify operational weaknesses.

* Improve SOPs based on actual employee performance.

* Help establish daily workflows.

* Create reporting procedures.

* Help establish ongoing quality-control processes.



Expected deliverables:



* Structured call center training system.

* Trained initial team of Virtual Assistants, subject to hiring and training timelines.

* Centralized SOP and training library.

* Daily and weekly workflow checklists.

* Employee performance tracking system.

* Recommendations for operational improvements.

* Initial outline of future digital marketing agency SOP requirements.



11. KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS (KPIs)



The Operations Assistant’s performance will be evaluated based on the quality, organization, and effectiveness of the operational systems developed.



Key performance indicators include:



1. SOP Completion: Number and quality of documented processes completed.

2. Video Training Production: Number of useful, organized training tutorials created.

3. Training Effectiveness: Ability of new Virtual Assistants to understand and perform their responsibilities.

4. Onboarding Efficiency: Ability to help new hires become productive using established training systems.

5. Documentation Accuracy: SOPs are clear, current, and easy to follow.

6. Workflow Organization: Daily processes are documented and consistently followed.

7. Administrative Accuracy: Minimal errors in assigned operational tasks.

8. Communication: Timely updates and effective coordination with management and employees.

9. Problem Identification: Ability to identify recurring operational problems and recommend solutions.

10. Process Improvement: Demonstrated improvements in efficiency and organization.

11. Team Support: Ability to assist employees and reduce unnecessary management involvement in routine training questions.

12. Agency Expansion Readiness: Ability to apply the same documentation and workflow-building skills to the digital marketing agency.



12. LONG-TERM GROWTH OPPORTUNITY



This position is intended to grow as our companies expand.



Initially, the Operations Assistant will focus primarily on Dump Serreno Junk Removal, Demolition & Excavation and the development of our virtual call center.



Once our initial team of 3–4 Virtual Assistants is operational and performing their responsibilities consistently, we will begin expanding the position into the operational development of our digital marketing agency.



The successful candidate will have the opportunity to take on additional responsibilities in:



* Operations coordination.

* SOP development and management.

* Employee onboarding and training.

* Workflow development.

* Process improvement.

* Administrative management.

* Cross-company operations support.



As the business grows, there may be opportunities to advance into a more senior Operations Coordinator or Operations Manager position, depending on performance, experience, and business needs.



13. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE



Our ultimate goal is to build a business that operates through organized systems, clearly defined responsibilities, and well-trained employees.



We want to create an environment where:



* Every recurring task has a documented process.

* Every employee understands their responsibilities.

* New employees can be trained using video tutorials and written SOPs.

* Inbound calls are handled professionally.

* Outbound calling activities are organized and tracked.

* Leads and customer information are documented correctly.

* Administrative tasks are completed consistently.

* Management can monitor operations through organized reports.

* Employees can find answers without constantly asking management how to perform routine tasks.

* New services, employees, and business divisions can be added without rebuilding the entire operational structure.



The Virtual Operations Assistant will play an important role in making this vision a reality.



14. HOW TO APPLY



Candidates interested in this position should provide:



1. A resume outlining previous administrative, virtual assistant, or operations experience.

2. A description of any experience creating SOPs or process documentation.

3. Examples of training videos, screen recordings, or tutorials they have created, if available.

4. A list of software platforms they have experience using.

5. A brief explanation of how they would approach learning a company’s back-office operations and turning those processes into a training system.



Candidates may also be asked to complete a practical assessment involving the creation of a simple SOP or screen-recorded tutorial.



We are looking for someone who wants to help build something, not simply someone looking for another administrative job.



We want a dependable, organized, motivated individual who can grow with our businesses and help us establish the systems necessary for long-term success.



My recommendation: How to structure this position



The person we hire will essentially be helping us build the operating manual for our companies.



Here is how I would divide the responsibilities over time:



Stage 1 – Build the foundation



Initial priority



Dumpster Rental, Junk Removal, Demolition & Excavation



* Learn all back-office processes.

* Create written and video SOPs.

* Document inbound and outbound calling.

* Build the administrative training library.

* Establish onboarding procedures.

    Stage 2 – Build the virtual team

    Hire and train 3–4 Virtual Assistants

* Train inbound call agents.

* Train outbound call agents.

* Train administrative assistants.

* Establish daily checklists.

* Monitor training progress and quality.

    Stage 3 – Stabilize operations

    Develop a repeatable call center operation

* Maintain SOPs.

* Improve workflows.

* Monitor performance reports.

* Help resolve operational bottlenecks.

* Reduce the owner’s involvement in routine training.

    Stage 4 – Expand into the digital marketing agency

    Future responsibility

    Develop the second business’s operating systems

* Create client onboarding SOPs.

* Document marketing production workflows.

* Develop project management procedures.

* Create employee training materials.

* Organize client communication and reporting.



Five additional recommendations before hiring



I would establish these expectations from the beginning:



1. Require video SOPs, not just written instructions. Every important software process should ideally have a screen-recorded demonstration. This will save considerable time when hiring additional employees.



2. Have the assistant learn by doing. Don’t just explain how the back office works. Have them perform the actual tasks, document each step, and then create the SOP.



3. Create one centralized company operations manual. Use Google Drive, Notion, or a similar platform to organize SOPs by department, job responsibility, and software.



4. Make the assistant responsible for training documentation, not automatically the entire call center’s sales performance. Initially, they should help train, monitor procedures, and report issues. You should retain authority over pricing, sales policies, and major customer decisions.



5. Make the digital marketing agency expansion a planned second phase. Don’t overload the assistant with both businesses before the first call center is properly established.

title: Payment Operations Chat Support Specialist | Remote, Part-Time
description:
ANGELICAGIO LLC is hiring a Philippines-based English chat support specialist for a long-term, remote part-time role. You'll help business customers by checking payment records, collecting missing information, updating customers on open cases, and escalating unresolved issues. We value reliable attendance, timely replies, and clear shift handovers. Team members who consistently perform well may be considered for a fixed full-time role as openings become available.



Schedule (Manila time, UTC+8)

Start with three days of paid training, planned at 10 hours per day.



Phase 1 — Days 1–10 after training

• Paid shifts: Tue 10:00–15:00; Wed 05:00–10:00; Fri 20:00–Sat 01:00; Sat 15:00–20:00.

• Emergency standby: Wed 03:00–05:00; Sat 01:00–03:00; Sun 01:00–03:00.

• A full week is 20 paid shift hours plus 6 standby hours. Your first 10 days follow the actual calendar dates.



Phase 2 — Day 11 onward

• Paid shifts: Tue 05:00–15:00; Fri 15:00–Sat 01:00.

• Emergency standby: Tue 03:00–05:00; Sat 01:00–03:00.

• Each full week is 20 paid shift hours plus 4 standby hours. Christmas and New Year coverage is scheduled separately.



Pay

Both phases use the same base rate of about USD 1.5385/hour. Pay is calculated per approved minute worked using USD 400 ÷ 26 ÷ 10 ÷ 60. USD 400 is the full-time-equivalent reference, and actual earnings depend on approved work time. Passive standby requires no time-tracker check-in. If called on to handle an urgent case, log the time worked for payment. Applicable pay premiums are handled separately.



Requirements and application

You need strong written English, attention to detail, a computer, reliable internet with a backup connection, and a power-outage plan. Customer support, BPO, fintech or e-commerce experience is preferred. Training covers the payment procedures.



HOW TO APPLY



1. Read both phases of the Manila-time schedule before applying.



2. Apply through OnlineJobs.ph with CHAT SUPPORT as the first line of your message. In that same message, include:

• Your current resume or a working resume link.

• Confirmation that you can cover the paid shifts and standby windows in both phases. Tell us which phase includes Sunday 01:00–03:00 standby.

• A short example in your own English of how you helped resolve a customer issue. Tell us what you checked and how you followed up. If you are new to support, an example from work, school, or volunteering is welcome.

• Your computer setup, backup internet connection, and plan for a power outage.



AFTER YOU APPLY



3. Check the
 associated with your OnlineJobs.ph application for an invitation from ANGELICAGIO LLC for job #
. Use your private link to confirm both schedules. The link is valid for three days.



4. Start the assessment within 24 hours of confirming your schedule. Once you select Start, you will have 25 minutes to answer five fictional payment-support scenarios in English. Save your answers as you go. We use the same exercise to review communication, payment checks, and follow-up consistently. HR reviews applicants who meet the role and assessment requirements.



The assessment is free. To verify the invitation, sign in to OnlineJobs.ph directly and check this job in your applications. The assessment page is hosted on Railway. It asks for your availability and written answers. Keep your assessment link private, along with passwords, verification codes, and banking details.

title: Construction Project Manager — Operations & Field Coordination
description:
Run the jobs. Own the outcome.

We are a growing construction company looking for a Construction Project Manager who takes a project from signed contract to final walkthrough and makes sure it lands safely, on schedule, on budget and to the quality our clients expect.

You will be the person everyone counts on: the link between management, clients, field crews, subcontractors and suppliers. If you like keeping several jobsites moving at the same time, protecting the budget and keeping clients informed, this role is for you.

Why you will want this role

• Report directly to the Owner / General Manager. Your input reaches the people who d
, with no layers in between.

• Real ownership. You run each project end to end: planning, crews, materials, subcontractors, budget, quality and closeout.

• Variety. Remodels, renovations, additions and general construction, never the same job twice.

• Clear processes. Defined SOPs, approval limits and weekly routines, so you always know what is expected and what happens next.

• Impact you can measure. Your success is tracked by clear KPIs: schedule adherence, budget performance, client satisfaction and more.

What you will do

1. Plan and schedule every project and build a clear execution plan before work starts.

2. Lead field crews across multiple active jobsites with daily assignments and progress checks.

3. Purchase and coordinate materials so nothing delays the job.

4. Control the budget. Track every cost, forecast the final number and flag overruns early.

5. Keep clients informed with at least weekly updates, and handle requests and concerns professionally.

6. Respond to new leads within one business day.

7. Coordinate subcontractors (electricians, plumbers, HVAC, roofers, flooring and other trades).

8. Manage scope and change orders, with written approval before any extra work.

9. Inspect quality and catch issues early.

10. Coordinate permits, inspections and compliance.

11. Oversee jobsite safety and organization.

12. Document and report project progress every week.

13. Close out projects with a finished punch list and a satisfied client.

What success looks like

• Organization: every project has a clear schedule, budget, scope and responsible team.

• Accountability: problems are identified, communicated and addressed before they escalate.

• Financial discipline: project costs are actively tracked, and spending decisions support expected profitability.

• Communication: clients, employees, subcontractors and management know what is expected and what happens next.

• Execution: projects move forward efficiently without unnecessary downtime or avoidable rework.

• Professionalism: client properties, company resources, employees and trade partners are treated respectfully.

How you will be measured

KPI Objective

Schedule Adherence Complete projects within approved timelines

Budget Performance Avoid unapproved cost overruns

Project Forecast Accuracy Identify financial and schedule risks early

Crew Utilization Minimize avoidable downtime

Material Availability Avoid delays caused by missing materials

Client Response Time Respond to leads and client inquiries within established standards

Client Satisfaction Maintain professional communication and resolve issues

Rework Rate Minimize quality-related corrections

Subcontractor Performance Meet quality, schedule and scope requirements

Documentation Compliance Maintain complete and accurate project records

Numerical KPI targets are established and approved by management.

________________________________________

The role in detail

Pre-construction

Before scheduling construction, you will:

• Review the signed contract and approved scope of work.

• Review project drawings, specifications and material selections.

• Obtain the approved internal project budget.

• Identify required trades, employees and subcontractors.

• Confirm the anticipated start and completion dates.

• Identify long-lead materials and potential project risks.

• Verify permit requirements and inspection dependencies.

• Clarify incomplete or conflicting information with management.

Outcome: a project execution plan with the necessary scope, budget, schedule, staffing and approvals.

Every approved project has an organized record with: client name and contact details; jobsite address; contract and approved scope of work; project budget and cost breakdown; assigned employees and subcontractors; project schedule and milestones; material selections and purchase records; permit and inspection information; progress photos and project notes; change orders and client approvals.

Construction does not begin without required authorization, permits and site readiness.

Crew scheduling and field coordination

• Prepare and maintain the weekly employee schedule.

• Assign employees according to project priorities, skills and availability.

• Coordinate employees across multiple active jobsites.

• Confirm the following day’s assignments in advance.

• Provide each crew with the jobsite address, reporting time, assigned tasks and relevant instructions.

• Adjust schedules when projects change or unexpected issues occur.

• Coordinate subcontractor schedules with the internal crew.

• Minimize idle time, unnecessary travel and scheduling conflicts.

Before work begins, make sure the crew understands: tasks to be performed; expected production goals; required materials and equipment; specific client instructions or property restrictions; safety considerations; and work that must be completed before another trade can begin.

Remain reachable during working hours and respond promptly to issues that could delay or interrupt work.

Obtain daily updates from the crew leader or responsible field employee (work completed, work remaining, attendance and hours, materials used or needed, problems encountered, photos of completed work, expected tasks for the next day). Compare actual progress with the approved schedule and address deviations.

Material purchasing and procurement

1. Review material requirements against the approved scope and budget.

2. Verify quantities, measurements, specifications and client-approved selections.

3. Check available inventory before purchasing.

4. Compare supplier pricing when appropriate.

5. Confirm management authorization according to the purchasing policy.

6. Place orders early enough to avoid construction delays.

7. Coordinate delivery dates and locations.

8. Verify material receipt, quantities, condition and discrepancies.

9. Record purchases and attach invoices or receipts to the correct project.

10. Coordinate returns, credits and unused materials.

Purchasing controls:

• All material purchases must be associated with a specific project or authorized company inventory.

• No unauthorized purchases may exceed the approved project allocation.

• Material substitutions affecting quality, appearance or client selections require appropriate approval.

• Unexpected material expenses must be reported before the purchase whenever feasible.

Budget and cost control

Track and categorize material expenses, employee labor costs, subcontractor costs, equipment and rental expenses, permits and inspection-related costs, disposal and transportation costs, and other project-related expenses.

At least weekly, review: original approved internal budget; approved budget adjustments; actual costs incurred; open purchase orders and committed expenses; estimated cost to complete; projected final cost; expected remaining budget.

Budget variance = Current approved budget − Projected final cost. A negative variance indicates a projected cost overrun.

If a project is expected to exceed its approved budget:

1. Identify the cause.

2. Determine the financial impact.

3. Notify management immediately.

4. Present corrective options where practical.

5. Obtain approval before committing additional discretionary spending.

6. Document the decision.

The PM may not independently increase the approved project budget. Cost savings must not compromise safety, code compliance, contractual specifications or approved quality standards.

Client communication and customer service

You are the primary operational contact for active projects. Keep clients informed about project progress, upcoming construction activities, schedule changes, material delays, required decisions or selections, inspection milestones, and issues that may affect the agreed scope, cost or timeline. Provide proactive updates at least weekly for active multi-day projects, or more often when necessary.

When a client requests a modification:

1. Confirm the exact request.

2. Determine whether it is included in the existing contract.

3. Assess the impact on materials, labor, cost and schedule.

4. Coordinate pricing and approval with management.

5. Obtain the required written change order.

6. Communicate approved instructions to the field crew.

Do not promise free additional work, revised completion dates or financial concessions without authorization.

For complaints and issues: acknowledge concerns promptly; gather accurate information before responding; coordinate appropriate corrective action; escalate significant disputes to management; document the concern and agreed resolution; confirm follow-through with the client.

Lead management and incoming inquiries

• Monitor assigned phone calls,
s, website inquiries and incoming messages.

• Respond to new leads within one business day.

• Collect customer contact information, property address, project type, timeline and general requirements.

• Determine whether the requested work falls within the company’s service area and capabilities.

• Schedule estimates or consultations with the appropriate person.

• Record lead information and follow-up activities.

• Follow up on pending inquiries and estimates as directed.

• Route technical pricing, contract negotiations and final sales decisions to authorized personnel.

Preparing or approving construction estimates is not automatically part of the PM’s authority unless expressly assigned by management.

Subcontractor management

You coordinate external trades including electricians, plumbers, HVAC technicians, roofers, flooring installers and other specialized contractors.

• Selection and preparation: identify required subcontractor work; request and compare quotes when applicable; verify that subcontractors meet company licensing and insurance requirements appropriate to their work and jurisdiction; confirm scope, pricing, timelines, exclusions and required deliverables; obtain management authorization before engaging new subcontractors or committing unapproved costs.

• Scheduling and execution: coordinate subcontractors with the master project schedule; confirm site readiness before arrival; provide approved drawings, work instructions and relevant site conditions; avoid scheduling conflicts between trades; monitor progress and adherence to the agreed scope; coordinate required inspections and follow-up work.

• Quality and payment verification: before recommending payment, verify that the billed work has been performed; review work quality and outstanding deficiencies; check invoices against the agreed pricing and approved changes; confirm appropriate documentation has been submitted; report disputes or incomplete work. Only authorized personnel may approve or release payments.

Quality control and jobsite oversight

• Conduct jobsite visits based on project complexity and risk.

• Verify that work follows approved plans, specifications and applicable requirements.

• Check alignment, dimensions, finishes, installation quality and workmanship.

• Identify deficiencies early.

• Assign corrective actions and verify completion.

• Maintain progress photos.

• Confirm the site is protected and reasonably clean.

• Coordinate proper protection of floors, furniture, fixtures and occupied areas.

• Prevent incomplete work from being concealed before required verification or inspection.

Permits, inspections and safety

Working with management and qualified personnel:

• Verify required permits before work begins.

• Track municipal inspections and approvals.

• Coordinate inspections at the appropriate construction stage.

• Address inspection corrections.

• Maintain inspection records.

• Ensure required licensed trades perform regulated work.

• Monitor visible safety concerns and site conditions.

• Escalate hazards, injuries, property damage and compliance issues immediately.

Safety-critical rule: stop or isolate work presenting imminent danger and notify the responsible supervisor or management. The PM’s oversight does not replace required competent-person supervision, trade licensing or designated safety responsibilities.

Change order management

Any work outside the approved scope follows the change order process:

1. Identify the requested or required change.

2. Document the reason and affected scope.

3. Obtain pricing and assess labor, material and subcontractor impacts.

4. Determine any schedule adjustment.

5. Submit for management review.

6. Obtain written client authorization where required.

7. Update the project budget and schedule.

8. Communicate the approved change to the field team.

9. Save all supporting documentation.

No extra work is performed without the necessary approval, except immediate actions needed to address a safety emergency or prevent further property damage, which must be escalated and documented.

Project closeout

• Verify that all contractual work is finished.

• Complete an internal quality inspection.

• Prepare and resolve the punch list.

• Schedule the final walkthrough with the customer.

• Coordinate final inspections and approvals where required.

• Verify completion of subcontractor work.

• Document remaining warranty or service items.

• Confirm the jobsite is clean and materials/equipment are removed.

• Organize final photos, permits, warranties and project documentation.

• Notify management that the project is ready for final billing and financial reconciliation.

The PM supports final billing but does not independently authorize invoice adjustments or refunds.

A day in the role

• Start of day: review active project schedules and priorities; confirm crew attendance and jobsite assignments; confirm subcontractor arrivals and planned work; review outstanding material deliveries; check client communications and new leads; resolve urgent field issues.

• Throughout the day: monitor progress across active jobsites; respond to crew and subcontractor questions; coordinate material purchases and deliveries; visit jobsites as required; communicate important changes to clients; track expenses and pending approvals; document delays, i
 and significant decisions.

• End of day: collect crew progress updates; record outstanding issues and next steps; review unfinished work and schedule impacts; confirm next-day employee assignments; confirm materials and subcontractors for the next day; update project records and management on urgent concerns.

Every week

• Review every active project’s schedule.

• Prepare the upcoming week’s crew assignments.

• Review budget versus actual and forecasted costs.

• Check subcontractor commitments and performance.

• Review pending material orders and delivery dates.

• Follow up on permits and inspections.

• Review outstanding change orders and client approvals.

• Provide progress updates to active clients.

• Identify projects at risk of delays or cost overruns.

• Submit a consolidated status report to management.

Weekly project status report (per active project):

Field Required information

Project Client / Jobsite

Status On Track / At Risk / Delayed

Progress Estimated % Complete

Schedule Planned vs. Forecast Completion

Budget Approved / Spent / Committed / Forecast

Crew Employees Assigned

Subcontractors Scheduled / Completed / Pending

Materials Ordered / Delivered / Outstanding

Issues Delays, Deficiencies, Client Concerns

Approvals Decisions Needed from Management

Next Steps Activities for the Upcoming Week

Authority and approval limits

You coordinate daily operations, but do not automatically have authority to:

• Approve project budget increases.

• Sign or modify client contracts.

• Commit to unapproved subcontractor agreements.

• Authorize purchases beyond delegated spending limits.

• Grant refunds or discounts.

• Approve additional work without required authorization.

• Change agreed project pricing.

• Promise completion dates unsupported by the approved schedule.

• Release company payments.

• Waive applicable quality, safety, permit or licensing requirements.

Management defines purchasing thresholds, subcontractor approval limits and escalation procedures in writing.

________________________________________

Your mission

Make sure the right people, materials, information and approvals are available at the right time, while keeping control of project costs, scheduling, quality and client communication. Proactively identify risks, escalate matters that need management approval and keep accurate records from start to finish.

The goal: quality construction projects delivered on time, within the approved budget, with a high level of client satisfaction.

Ready to apply?

Send your resume and a short note about the construction projects you have managed: project type, budget size and your role

title: Ecommerce Marketing Specialist
description:
We are a leading homewares and interiors Australian Ecommerce business.



We are looking for an excellent marketer who has embraced AI, not someone who believes using AI makes them a marketing expert.



The successful candidate will have a strong foundation in marketing principles, substantial professional experience and the ability to critically assess the work that AI produces.



They will be responsible for ensuring marketing initiatives are delivered accurately, efficiently and with measurable commercial outcomes.



2. The Role

The position combines 5 key areas of responsibility:



-
 marketing and customer lifecycle management.

-
 subscriber acquisition and lead generation.

- SMS marketing execution and cost control.

- SEO and organic search execution.

- Shopify website management and conversion rate optimisation support.



These functions will be supported by our evolving AI operating environment, primarily using Claude AI and integrations with our existing technology platforms.



The Founder will provide overarching marketing direction, brand strategy, commercial priorities and approval of significant initiatives.



The successful candidate will be expected to independently manage day-to-day execution, identify opportunities, interpret performance data and continually improve results.



OVERVIEW OF AREAS OF FOCUS



1.
 Marketing and Lifecycle Management

Platforms: Maestra, Claude AI, Figma



 marketing is a core responsibility of this position. The successful candidate will manage the execution, monitoring and ongoing optimisation of our
 marketing programme. We are implementing AI-assisted workflows that enable campaign designs to be converted from Figma into
 builds, with AI supporting audience segmentation, content personalisation, reporting and performance analysis.



You will manage the execution of our
 marketing calendar, ensuring campaigns are built, tested, approved and scheduled correctly. You will also ensure correct audience targeting, segmentation, exclusions and frequency management.



Maintain automated lifecycle flows, including welcome, browse abandonment, cart abandonment, checkout abandonment, post-purchase and reactivation. Review AI-generated performance analysis to identify underperforming campaigns and flows.



Refresh creative assets, messaging and campaign structures based on performance insights.



Develop and execute ongoing A/B testing across subject lines, messaging, creative, calls to action and segmentation.



Monitor
 deliverability, engagement, unsubscribes, conversion and revenue.





2.
 Subscriber Acquisition and Lead Generation

This is one of the highest commercial priorities of the role.



We want to build a substantially stronger approach to acquiring new, relevant subscribers and growing our engaged
 audience.



Our initial acquisition target is approximately 6,000 new
 subscribers per month, with an emphasis on quality, engagement and eventual purchasing behaviour.



The successful candidate must proactively develop and execute subscriber acquisition initiatives rather than simply maintain the existing database. You will develop and maintain an ongoing pipeline of lead generation initiatives. Optimise pop-ups, sign-up forms, landing pages and other acquisition touchpoints. Coordinate lead generation partnerships, competitions and other appropriate acquisition initiatives.





3. SMS Marketing



SMS is an important marketing channel but carries significant direct costs. Accuracy, attention to detail and strict financial controls are essential. You will prepare and schedule approved SMS campaigns.





4. SEO and Organic Search



We currently operate an AI-supported SEO workflow that produces regular audits, recommendations and prioritised tasks. The successful candidate will be responsible for reviewing these findings, validating their relevance and implementing approved recommendations. You will review weekly AI-generated SEO audits and task recommendations. You will optimise product pages, collection pages, metadata and internal linking. You will use AI to Identify technical SEO issues and coordinate fixes with our Shopify developer.







5. Shopify Website Management and CRO Support



Strong practical Shopify experience is essential. The successful candidate must be confident working within the Shopify backend and performing routine ecommerce website management tasks. You will maintain and update product information, descriptions, imagery and merchandising. Create and update collection pages, landing pages and relevant website content. You must support promotional campaign execution, including checking pricing, promotional messaging and product presentation.



Essential Qualifications and Experience

We require an experienced, professionally trained digital marketer who has more recently embraced artificial intelligence to enhance their existing expertise.



We are not recruiting an entry-level employee, a general virtual assistant or someone whose principal skill is generating marketing content with AI.



Ideally 4–6 years of genuine, hands-on digital marketing experience.



Previous experience working with an established direct-to-consumer ecommerce brand.



Demonstrated experience managing
 campaigns, customer segmentation and automated lifecycle programmes.



Practical Shopify backend experience.

title: Business Strategy & Development Officer
description:
WE'RE LOOKING FOR A BUSINESS BUILDER



We are building a new kind of engineering consultancy, one designed around engineering, technology, efficiency and an improved client experience.



We are looking for someone who wants to help build it with us.



Working directly with senior leadership, the Business Strategy & Development Officer will help turn the company's vision into an operating business. This will involve strategy, research, business planning, process development, technology implementation, client-experience development and ultimately regional growth.



This is not primarily a sales role.



We are looking for someone who can take an idea, research it, challenge it, structure it, develop a plan and help drive that plan through implementation.



The successful candidate will help develop the company's:



Business strategy and implementation roadmap

Operating model and business processes

Technology strategy

Digital client experience

Corporate systems and procedures

Business plans and financial models

Market and competitor research

Performance-management framework

New business opportunities

Regional expansion strategy



The role will also coordinate external specialists involved in areas such as branding, technology, websites, digital systems and corporate services.



We're particularly interested in candidates who are:



Analytical.

 Strategic.

 Technology-minded.

 Highly organized.

 Excellent researchers.

 Strong professional writers.

 Comfortable working independently.

 Naturally curious about how businesses work.

 Capable of taking ownership of complex initiatives.



A degree in Business, Management, Economics, Finance, Entrepreneurship or a related discipline is preferred.



Experience in business consulting, strategy, project management, professional services, technology or business transformation would be particularly valuable.



This is intended to be a long-term career opportunity.



The initial objective is to help build and implement the new company. As the business grows, the position is intended to develop into Business Strategy & Development Manager, with increasing responsibility for strategic initiatives, supporting staff and regional expansion throughout the Caribbean.

title: Events Coordinator
description:
The company

A private, application-only membership community for founders and business owners, operating across several US markets. Members meet at invitation-only social events, stay connected through a members-only mobile app, and receive curated one-to-one introductions.



What this role is

You run the event calendar. The flagship is a recurring invitation-only evening event held in each market every other month, which means an event somewhere roughly every two weeks, plus virtual sessions members get each week. The bar is high: small rooms, hand-picked guests, rooftops and pool decks, no name badges and no conference energy. Your job is to keep that calendar full, those rooms full, and the founders on schedule.



Venue sourcing and event production

- Find and secure venues that fit a premium brand: rooftops, pool decks, private rooms in strong hotels and restaurants, spaces that photograph well

- Cold outreach to venues, GMs and event managers: pitch, negotiate rate or comp, hold the date, close it

- Build a standing venue shortlist in each market so the next event is never a scramble

- Own the run of show: timing, check-in, food and beverage, vendors, AV where needed

- Keep a forward calendar across all markets so dates lock months out, not weeks



Guest list and attendance

- Curate the invite list per event. Who is in the room matters more than how many.

- Run the RSVP push across SMS,
 and in-app notifications

- Chase RSVPs person by person until the room is full. No blast and hope.

- Follow up after each event: thank-yous, feedback, re-engagement of no-shows



Virtual sessions

- Run the weekly cadence: a mastermind and an industry roundtable on alternating weeks

- Group the right members onto each industry call by sector and stage

- Line up and brief the guest for each session

- Send invites, confirm the roster, chase attendance



Promotion and creator outreach

- Reach out to creators and partners who can post about events and bring the right people

- Keep event listings and in-app content current

- Pull usable material out of every event: photos, clips, recaps



- Follow-through

- Track what the founders and the team owe each event, and chase it

- Hold people to their dates, warmly and persistently

- Flag risk early: venue unconfirmed, RSVPs light, no guest booked



Required

- Two or more years running events, community programs, or high-touch coordination

- Venue sourcing and negotiation experience, with specific spaces secured and terms achieved

- A track record of filling rooms, with real attendance numbers

- Brand judgment. Can tell a venue that fits a premium membership brand from one that does not.

- Excellent spoken and written English, confident cold-calling US venue managers and talking with founders

- Interpersonal warmth paired with the backbone to hold people to commitments

- Highly organized, works from a system, never needs reminding twice



Nice to have

- Hospitality, nightlife, or private-club events background

- Experience inside a membership or founder community

- Light content work: recaps, social posts, short clips

- Comfortable in CRM tools, SMS platforms, and mobile app admin



Very nice to have

- Has procured vendor or brand sponsorships for events, and can name what they closed and on what terms

- Has negotiated content or media partnership deals

We're looking for a (Senior) Dispute Manager who lives and breathes payment disputes, knows exactly how to win them (and prevent them), and can fully own this role from day one.

This role is for an A-player who takes ownership not someone we need to micromanage.



You should be able to walk into our environment, understand it fast, and know exactly how to operate from your own experience. We'll give you a clear SOP, but we're not looking for someone we have to hand-hold or explain the basics to. You'll run this function independently keeping our payment processors healthy without the store manager or backend manager having to chase you. If you need constant direction, this isn't the role. If you want to take real ownership and help us scale to big numbers, keep reading.



What you'll do:



Own and drive down our dispute/chargeback rate across Shopify Payments, PayPal, Klarna, and Whop

Respond to and win disputes, chargebacks, and pre-arbitration cases with strong, evidence-backed submissions

Spot patterns early and put systems in place to prevent disputes before they happen

Work closely with our customer support and backend teams to protect our payment processors and keep them healthy

Report on dispute KPIs and continuously improve win rates



What we're looking for:



3+ years of hands-on experience as a dispute manager in ecommerce — specifically dropshipping stores (this is a must)

Deep, proven experience handling disputes on PayPal and Klarna ( WHOP a big plus)

A track record of actually lowering dispute and chargeback rates — not just submitting forms

Someone who takes full ownership of their role and thrives without micromanagement

Strong written English and sharp attention to detail

Reliable, self-driven, and able to work independently within a team



What we offer:



A spot on a fast-growing, multi-market team where you can genuinely grow into higher positions

KPI-based bonuses on top of your base pay — the better your results, the more you earn

Flexibility — work around your schedule

A long-term project, not a one-off gig 



Hours & commitment:



5 days a week, ~4 hours/day on average (flexes between 2–6 hours on lighter days and up to 6-8 hours on busy ones, depending on workload)

We need someone who can start right away



If you know how to keep payment processors healthy, take ownership, and turn disputes into wins, we want to talk.



If you have worked for stores that generated over 50K Monthly revenue, please let us your top 3 stores know so we can validate this if it is a store that needs management on high level.



To apply: Start your proposal with the word "DISPUTE MANAGER" and tell us, in one or two sentences, a specific example of a dispute/chargeback rate you brought down — and how. Bonus points if you tell us how you'd take ownership of a function like this without needing to be managed.
